sections.body: The Clover Co-op climbs the trunk of an ancient tree, level stacked on level, crowded with music and good-natured noise. A friendly local stops you at the door: newcomers hang their shoes on the line strung across the ground floor. By the time you leave, locals promise, the shoes come back shined and filled with little trinkets. Warmth, food, and a dozen conversations wait. What do you do?

Publicobjective: Rest, connect, and become someone the town trusts.

Readaloud: The Clover Co-op climbs the trunk of an ancient tree, level stacked on level, crowded with music and good-natured noise. A friendly local stops you at the door: newcomers hang their shoes on the line strung across the ground floor. By the time you leave, locals promise, the shoes come back shined and filled with little trinkets. Warmth, food, and a dozen conversations wait. What do you do?
Gmnotes: This scene is relationship, not objective extraction. Slow down and let players be people. Do not turn hospitality into shopping inventory; use gifts as story boons.
Gmscript: Say: "This is Hush's living room. Hang your shoes if you want to honor the custom. Pick a face, pick a table, or tell me one thing this tavern has that no tavern outside Hush would have."
Gmreadaloud: The Clover Co-op climbs the trunk of an ancient tree. Newcomers hang their shoes on the line strung across the ground floor. Warmth, food, and a dozen conversations wait.

Gmchecklist: Offer the shoe custom and reward it later with polished, trinket-filled shoes. Describe Fidget, Lausa, and Halython before naming them. Ask one player-authored tavern prompt. Offer Prepare/Hope as a quiet breather. Let Halython ask about the road outcome when the moment is warm.
Gmprivate: Halython's Bramble question lets bramble_outcome affect trust without lore-dumping. Even the tavern has small protective wards; Marlowe can notice this.
Playertakeaway: This is the warm center of the act: a place to be people before being couriers again.
Storytakeaway: Belonging in Hush is offered through customs, food, games, and careful attention.
Mechanictakeaway: Downtime is mechanical here: Prepare/Hope, Presence, and respectful roleplay can raise hush_trust and unlock a guide.

Relationshipprompts: Which PC quietly checks on someone else here? Who disagrees about the right thing to do without breaking trust?
Ownershipprompt: Name one detail in The Clover Co-op that belongs to your character's point of view.

Fearspends: Spend Fear to make trust cost time, reveal a local fear, or show a ward symptom that locals have normalized. Make trust cost time, humility, or a public apology. Show a ward symptom locals have normalized because nobody official listened.

Choicesconsequences: Honor the shoe custom The room relaxes; later the shoes return shined with small trinkets. Raise or reinforce hush_trust. Lootclues: Use Clover Co-op gifts table Sableleaf Shoes: A pair of shoes sewn entirely from broad sablewood leaves sits light as breath, green-veined, and already leaning toward motion. Bugbane Berry™: A fat red-orange berry shines a little too perfectly, with a tiny insect suspended dead-center like a pit in amber. It looks appetizing and deeply wrong. Sable Sap: Warm amber sap beads from a crack in a huge trunk like the tree is breathing it out. It smells of honey, woodsmoke, and something older. Fire Wine™: A strong golden liquor sloshes in a thick jug, warm going down and warmer staying there. A paper tag insists it is not made from grapes and is absolutely not medicinal.

Storyscope: Perceived antagonist: the forest. True antagonist: the corporate lie about the forest. The players never confront it directly. They are meant to feel it by the end. Every act offers at least one guaranteed and one earned hint that the danger is manufactured and the forest is not the enemy. A Grail "Protection Coverage" invoice hangs on the Clover Co-op wall, overdue and steep. ADD GUARANTEED Firstmoss and the Sunless Farms show the forest feeding Hush rather than hunting it. REFLAVOR GUARANTEED An elder says, "The wood was never this bad. The trouble came with the waymarkers." ADD EARNED Presence Easy 10 A ledger shows protection costs and hazard sightings climbing together. ADD EARNED Knowledge Medium 15 A Grail "Protection Coverage" invoice hangs on the Clover Co-op wall, overdue and steep. ADD GUARANTEED Presence: get people talking. Knowledge: read invoice/ledger. Instinct: sense resentment under hospitality.
